Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

ready adjective

also are you ready?, get ready, I’m ready

classical

Ter. Heaut. 2.3.114: tibi erunt parāta verba (Lewis & Short s.v. parō)
Traupman 369

parātus, parāta, parātum

Declension on Wiktionary

The participle of parāre, prepare. Of a person, “ready to” takes the infinitive or ad + acc.

Other words

  • promptus, prompta, promptum — ready, quick, willing

    also used · classical · Caes. BC 1.3: laudat promptōs (Lewis & Short s.v. prōmō); Traupman 69 · Declension on Wiktionary

    Lewis & Short: “at hand, prepared, ready, quick, prompt”; it stresses willingness more than parātus does.

Examples

  • Esne prompta?

    Are you ready?Traupman 69

See also prepare, at your service.

SourcesLewis & Short: paro · Lewis & Short: promo

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
